metadata.name: Luxemburgism (democratic revolutionary Marxism)
metadata.description: Luxemburg’s democratic revolutionary Marxism, combining mass participation, political freedom, social ownership and international solidarity.
metadata.scope: Luxemburg’s democratic, mass-participatory revolutionary Marxism, reconstructed from her writings and scholarship. The profile preserves her rejection of narrow nationalism and bureaucratic substitution for workers’ action. It does not attribute contemporary government conduct or the policies of later parties to her. This is a sourced interpretation of the specified tradition, not an adherent questionnaire. Unresolved evidence or an unrepresented institutional premise is recorded as unknown, never as numerical neutrality. Historical sources are not treated as answers to modern technologies by analogy. Government acts are contextual evidence only, not a substitute for the scoped doctrine. The December 1918 Spartacus programme is included: it demands a council republic with a working-population franchise, not unrestricted liberal parliamentary competition. This qualifies, rather than erases, Luxemburg’s defence of dissent in The Russian Revolution.
metadata.phrase: A socialist society developed through workers’ mass participation, political freedom and international solidarity.

axes.counterEvidence: The revision 1 answer set exceeded its evidence. The original source selection omitted the concrete December 1918 Spartacus programme, which substantially qualifies the liberal-democratic reading. Its council franchise covers the working population; that is not the question’s unconditional every-adult vote. Its programme replaces parliamentary institutions and joins supreme executive and legislative power in the central council; freedom-of-dissent passages cannot erase this. Marx’s Theses and Gotha are contextual sources, not direct evidence for Luxemburg’s particular causal or benefit-policy answers. All banks are expropriated in the programme, not maintained alongside private banks.
